data.content_ref: inline:The target's mechanism contains an internal contradiction that defeats its own claim. The claim asserts that the scientific preference is 'defensible as a systemic feature,' but the mechanism concludes that 'the underlying structure was never relevant to the outcome at all.' The preference being defended is precisely a preference for better-corroborated theories — i.e., a preference grounded in the evidential structure relating theories to observations. If that underlying structure is irrelevant to the outcome of the selection process, then the evolutionary mechanism has no basis for selecting better-corroborated theories over arbitrary alternatives; the systemic feature would be unconnected to any epistemically significant property. The target cannot simultaneously defend the preference as a meaningful systemic feature and declare the structure that constitutes the preference irrelevant to the outcome. This is distinct from prior objections about individual vs. systemic justification: it is an internal inconsistency within the target's own systemic account.
